definitions.fully-matched: Fully matched or retained approved real example

important: Accounting is not photographic coverage. Fully-matched retains approved limited real examples with their disclosed differences; only the separate direct-match count means direct matches. Remaining cases are not approved links. Metadata-only leads are not image inspections. Unmatched does not mean no equivalent exists. Further suitable human photographs may exist.

records.title: Skull base, external (inferior) view
records.reason: The unpainted dry human cranium is photographed from the inferior external base with mandible and atlas absent. Fine foramina are unlabelled; laterality is immaterial here.

records.title: Cranial floor, internal (superior) view
records.reason: A genuine dry human cranium is shown from the internal cranial-floor aspect; named openings remain unlabelled but the depicted floor and fossae are present.

records.title: Cranial sutures: superior and posterior views
records.reason: Superior human dry skull photo confirms the sagittal/coronal suture view and a separate human posterior lambda detail confirms the lambdoid junction. The detail is not a full posterior skull view.

records.title: Typical vertebra: superior view with lateral inset
records.reason: A dry human thoracic vertebra in superior view shows the common vertebral plan. The assigned thoracic lateral inset, disc, and separate detail are not shown.

records.title: Atlas (C1) from above and axis (C2) from the side
records.reason: The human dry atlas and axis pair is photographed from above, but the assigned C2 lateral view is absent.

records.title: Thoracic cage, anterior view
records.reason: Targeted searches found no visually inspected dry human rib-cage photo with the sternum and cartilage arrangement. A Calisphere anterior human thorax dissection page surfaced and its caption was fetched, but the photograph itself was not visually inspected and the complete bone/cartilage plate cannot be confirmed; this is unavailable evidence, not proof that no suitable photo exists.

records.title: Rib detail: head, tubercle and costal groove
records.reason: Two targeted searches yielded no visually inspected, provenance-checked human rib specimen photo showing the head, tubercle and costal groove; candidate illustrations/renders were excluded.

records.title: Right scapula: anterior (left) and posterior (right)
records.reason: Separate photographed human scapula specimens provide the anterior and posterior surfaces, with the coracoid/glenoid side and posterior spine/acromion respectively visible. Side and same-bone identity are not stated; that is a real-example limitation, not a missing view.

records.title: Pectoral girdle relationships, anterior view (right side detailed)
records.reason: Scapular surface photographs and a right anterior human glenohumeral dissection establish portions of the girdle. Clavicle, complete clavicle-scapula-humerus relationships, and ligament set are not covered.

records.title: Right humerus: anterior (left) and posterior (right)
records.reason: Verified human dry-humerus specimen photos show complete anterior and posterior aspects. They do not establish that both views are the same right bone; laterality/pair identity is disclosed as unconfirmed.

records.title: Right forearm, anterior view, with proximal-ulna inset
records.reason: A real human articulated radius-ulna specimen is shown anteriorly at the elbow. It is not the complete right forearm, interosseous membrane, or proximal-ulna lateral inset.

records.title: Right hand, palmar view: carpals, metacarpals, phalanges
records.reason: An assembled human hand skeleton photo covers carpals, metacarpals and phalanges. The source does not identify palmar/dorsal orientation or side, so it is not claimed as an exact right-palmar match.

records.title: Right hip bone: lateral (left) and medial (right) views
records.reason: A dry human os coxae lateral view shows acetabulum and obturator foramen; a hip-joint dissection supplies limited context. Medial surface and laterality are unverified.

records.title: Right femur: anterior (left) and posterior (right)
records.reason: The one dry human femur is shown in anterior and posterior views, including posterior linea aspera; side is not stated, so a right-sided specimen is not claimed.

records.title: Right leg, anterior view, with tibial-plateau inset
records.reason: A dry human tibia/fibula anterior pair corresponds to the main leg bones. The superior plateau inset, ankle mortise detail, and laterality are not documented.

records.title: Right foot, dorsal view: tarsals, metatarsals, phalanges
records.reason: Reinspection confirms a real assembled human foot with exposed dorsal tarsal surfaces, all three cuneiforms, metatarsals and phalanges; the first toe has two phalanges. The view is oblique and the toes point down the photograph, unlike the toes-up schematic. Side is not stated by the source and is not asserted in the link.

records.title: Generic synovial joint in section
records.reason: A photographed human left elbow dissection is a specific synovial-joint example, not a generic section proving the full capsule, synovial lining/fluid, and external ligament layers.

records.title: Right shoulder joint relationships, anterior view
records.reason: A right anterior glenohumeral dissection opens the capsule and exposes the glenoid fossa. It does not cover the complete shoulder bones and ligament relationships in the diagram.

records.title: Right knee: anterior layer (left) and deep cruciates, patella omitted (right)
records.reason: Verified left medial knee and posterior popliteal-fossa dissections show joint structures and PCL. The anterior right-knee panel and full cruciate/collateral set remain incomplete; a newly surfaced right anterior Calisphere candidate was not visually inspected.

records.title: Anterior anatomical position
records.reason: No actual human photograph in the standardized anterior anatomical stance, with palms forward and thumbs lateral, was visually verified. Search surfaced mostly schematic position illustrations.

records.title: Posterior anatomical position
records.reason: No matching standardized posterior-view human photograph was verified; available anatomical-position results were schematic.

records.title: Three body planes compared
records.reason: Three named human regional examples now cover sagittal, coronal and transverse planes. These demonstrate orientation conventions, not a literal three-plane cut through one whole human body. The transverse reference is explicitly medical imaging rather than a specimen photograph.

records.title: Major body cavities with serous-space inset
records.reason: No single verified human photograph covers the cavities, diaphragm, retroperitoneal kidney, and pleural-space inset. Sectional candidates did not meet this composite coverage.

records.title: Four abdominal quadrants
records.reason: Four quadrant boundaries are a surface-location convention, not physical specimen boundaries. This justifies no literal photograph; it does not make the underlying organs unphotographable.

records.title: Nine abdominal regions
records.reason: The nine-region grid is an imposed surface-location convention, not nine physical specimen partitions. A body photograph alone would not depict these boundaries.

records.title: Whole-body organ locations
records.reason: No one verified human in-situ photograph shows the full set of labeled organs and retroperitoneal kidneys. A valid composite needs separately verified subject-specific sources.

records.title: Anterior skeleton
records.reason: Verified human dry-bone photos give selected anterior skull, scapula, femur, tibia/fibula, hand, and foot examples. They do not form a complete articulated skeleton or include the full rib cage and other bones.

records.title: Posterior skeleton
records.reason: Verified dry human photos show a posterior scapula and anterior/posterior femur pair. Most posterior axial and appendicular regions are absent.

records.title: Axial and appendicular skeleton
records.reason: The selected real specimens include skull and thoracic vertebra examples for axial bones, plus scapula, femur, tibia/fibula, hand and foot examples for appendicular bones. The hand and foot source pages were individually visually confirmed in their bone-specific records; this collection still does not form a complete skeleton or demonstrate the full division.

records.title: Anterior skull: facial bones and openings
records.reason: A genuine anterior human skull specimen is verified. It is worn and unlabelled, so minor facial foramina and some boundaries are not clearly represented.

records.title: Left lateral skull
records.reason: No exact human dry-bone lateral skull photograph with credible specimen provenance and visual inspection was verified. The newly fetched similarly titled Commons candidate credits a medical illustrator and cannot be relied upon as a genuine dry bone specimen.

records.title: Lateral vertebral column plate
records.reason: No photographed dry human vertebral column with credible specimen provenance was verified; previously inspected display-column imagery did not establish a human dry-bone specimen.

records.title: Regional vertebrae compared: cervical, thoracic, lumbar (superior view)
records.reason: Human dry cervical and thoracic vertebra examples are verified in superior-compatible views. No comparable lumbar specimen or complete three-region comparison is present.

records.title: Original anatomical planes
records.reason: Sagittal and coronal human brain sections plus an axial human MRI give specifically named real examples of all three plane conventions. These are regional brain examples and different individuals, not a whole-body photographic reconstruction.

records.title: Original body cavities
records.reason: No verified human section photograph meets the composite body-cavity/diaphragm coverage; a page describing the NLM dataset is not an inspected specimen image.

records.title: Elbow joint
records.reason: A verified human elbow joint dissection is a relevant real example, but it does not reproduce all the original illustration labels and cross-sectional layers.

records.title: Pelvis
records.reason: A frontal dry human pelvis photo shows both hip bones and sacrum; the assigned plate includes additional structures and landmarks, including attached femora, that are missing.

records.title: Axial skeleton, anterior view
records.reason: Verified photos cover anterior skull, cranial floor and a thoracic vertebra. A complete axial skeleton, ribs and full vertebral column are not covered.

records.title: Appendicular skeleton, anterior view
records.reason: Verified human specimens cover selected scapula, femur, tibia/fibula, hand and foot bones. They do not form the full appendicular skeleton and hand/foot laterality/view limits remain.

records.title: Deep back muscles (trapezius and latissimus dorsi removed)
records.reason: Partial: human posterior deep-back and right scapular dissection photographs verify multifidus/rotator and scapular-region examples, but they do not jointly show the assigned unilateral lumbar quadratus lumborum plus intact-versus-removed erector spinae comparison.

records.title: Posterior arm and elbow
records.reason: Posterior arm photographs show deltoid, teres major and long/lateral triceps heads; the deep arm shows medial triceps and radial nerve. Posterior forearm image 15 explicitly labels anconeus at the elbow. Separate dissections, not the same donor or guaranteed same side as the drawing; the anconeus detail is on the posterior-forearm photograph.

records.title: Forearm: anterior and posterior views
records.reason: Anterior images identify pronator teres and flexor carpi radialis. Posterior superficial image 15 identifies extensor carpi radialis longus/brevis and anconeus; deep image 17 identifies supinator. Several dissected layers on one teaching page, not a single intact right forearm or matched donor.

records.title: Abdominal wall layers
records.reason: The previously inspected human dissection depicts all four required muscles: rectus abdominis, external oblique, internal oblique and transversus abdominis. A single layered left anterolateral field is a suitable limited real example; three separate schematic panels and identical orientation are not required.

records.title: Gluteal region: surface and cutaway
records.reason: Posterior specimens show superficial gluteus maximus and gluteus medius, followed by reflected maximus exposing medius and the deeper gluteal region. The source reflects rather than entirely removes maximus; donor and side are not asserted to match the illustration.

records.title: Deep thigh: anterior and posterior cutaways
records.reason: Partial: the verified human right anterior thigh photo supports the vastus-intermedius region, but the source does not establish the full articularis-genus detail or the posterior semimembranosus cutaway.

records.title: Anterior and lateral leg
records.reason: Anterolateral leg shows tibialis anterior and its tendon; the lateral leg identifies fibularis longus and brevis, with their paths toward the ankle and dorsal foot. The comparison uses anterior and lateral photographs, not one schematic frontal view; side and donor identity are not matched.

records.title: Calf: surface and cutaway
records.reason: Partial: the inspected human specimen photograph directly shows the gastrocnemius–soleus junction, but it is an isolated medial specimen and does not include in-situ popliteus or tibialis posterior.

records.title: Hand: intrinsic muscles, palmar view
records.reason: Thenar dissection identifies abductor pollicis brevis and flexor pollicis brevis. Hypothenar dissection identifies abductor digiti minimi (cut), and image 12 shows lumbricals arising alongside the deep flexor tendons. Abductor digiti minimi is cut to expose deeper muscles; separate layers and specimens are shown rather than the intact right-hand arrangement.

records.title: Foot: plantar first layer and dorsal inset
records.reason: Partial: two inspected Stanford photos confirm left plantar human specimens and deep plantar structures, but neither shows the assigned first plantar layer (abductor hallucis/flexor digitorum brevis) and the separate dorsal extensor-digitorum-brevis inset is not covered.

records.title: Pelvic floor: levator ani, superior view
records.reason: Partial: a verified human male perineum/pelvic-diaphragm photograph names levator ani, but its perineal/superior fascia view does not match the assigned superior pelvic-floor view or establish the pubococcygeus and iliococcygeus bands.

records.title: Face and neck muscles, right lateral view
records.reason: Partial: distinct inspected human face and left lateral-neck dissection photos offer regional examples, but named facial-muscle coverage is incomplete and the neck side/view does not match the right lateral composite.

records.title: Anterior chest and shoulder muscles
records.reason: Partial: human anterior thorax and right axilla source photos verify pectoral/intercostal examples, but not the full asymmetric superficial-to-deep chest, shoulder and abdominal muscle plate.

records.title: Anterior arm: superficial and deep layers
records.reason: Superficial anterior arm identifies deltoid and both biceps heads. A deeper dissection with biceps tendons cut exposes coracobrachialis and brachialis; forearm images identify pronator teres and flexor carpi radialis. Several photographs cover the two drawing panels. Biceps tendons are cut in the deep image; not a matched right-sided donor.

records.title: Anterior thigh: superficial layer
records.reason: Anterior thigh series shows sartorius, quadriceps and tensor fasciae latae; the deeper image identifies iliopsoas, vastus medialis/lateralis and cut rectus femoris. Medial views show adductor longus and gracilis. This is a set of single-limb dissections, not the bilateral superficial plate; some muscles are cut or reflected to expose deeper anatomy.

records.title: Superficial back and scapular muscles
records.reason: Partial: the inspected LibreTexts/BlueLink page includes one actual superficial posterior cadaver-back photo, but its letter markers are not independently decoded and not all assigned scapular structures are confirmed.

records.title: Posterior lower limb: contextual overview
records.reason: Partial: an inspected left posterolateral thigh photograph verifies gluteal and hamstring-region examples, but no retained source establishes the bilateral posterior overview through the calf and all depicted structures.

records.title: Superficial muscles, anterior and posterior views
records.reason: Partial: specific right shoulder/back, left posterior-lateral thigh/gluteal and anterior thorax source photographs provide regional examples, but no source set forms the whole-body paired superficial views or establishes all pinned muscles.

records.title: Diaphragm: domes and inferior view
records.reason: Partial: Stanford's inspected human superior and inferior diaphragm photos verify those real views, but the assigned anterior coronal cutaway and comparative dome-height panel are missing.

records.title: Rotator cuff: anterior and posterior views
records.reason: Posterior shoulder identifies supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor and teres major. The anterior shoulder identifies subscapularis; the opened superficial tissues expose the cuff and joint capsule. Complementary dissected views; no claim of the same specimen or laterality as the schematic.

records.title: Optic disc, macula and optic nerve head
records.reason: Partial: Compared the fundus panel with a human fundus photograph and human optic-nerve-head histology. A fundus image does not show the nerve-head cutaway; macular/foveal detail and permission-qualified figure panels remain limitations.

records.title: Brain, lateral surface: lobes and insula
records.reason: Partial: Compared the lateral-lobe/insula diagram with one human lateral-dissection candidate and a verified medial-section photo. Candidate caption shows resected lateral cortex, but image inspection and exposed insula are not established.

records.title: Brain, midsagittal view: callosum, diencephalon, ventricles
records.reason: The actual medial brain section shows corpus callosum, the diencephalic region and ventricular spaces above the midbrain, pons, medulla and sectioned cerebellum. A second ventricular view explicitly identifies lateral, third and fourth ventricles. The small hypothalamic/epithalamic structures and aqueduct are not individually labeled in these photographs. Fixed tissue and section plane differ from the schematic; this is a real regional comparison, not a substitute labeled answer key.

records.title: Eye in section: tunics, lens and vitreous chamber
records.reason: Partial: Compared full-eye section diagram against the available human fundus example only; it does not show cornea, tunics, lens or vitreous section. Full globe photo not verified.

records.title: Ear in section: outer, middle and inner
records.reason: Partial: Compared ear-section diagram against the NLM historical human-ear photographic-work catalog. Catalog-level record lacks a reviewed individual plate; outer/middle/inner coverage remains unverified.

records.title: Spinal cord cross-section specimen
records.reason: The real transverse human vertebral-column section includes the spinal cord, with central gray matter and peripheral white matter explicitly identified. Gross donor section rather than a stained micrograph. This establishes the linked comparison as human; it does not retrospectively establish the organism of Boneefied's existing source image.

records.title: Deep brain nuclei, coronal slice
records.reason: Partial: Compared the coronal nuclei diagram with a human pathological coronal gross section. Source caption is edema, not basal nuclei; caudate, putamen and pallidum are not identified.

records.title: Brainstem, cerebellum and spinal cord, midsagittal
records.reason: Medial brain section shows the labeled midbrain, pons and medulla with the sectioned cerebellar arbor vitae and fourth ventricular space. The brain is separated from its cord. Use the separately named cord dissection for the spinal-cord subject of the composite drawing.

records.title: Ventricles, CSF and meninges
records.reason: Partial: Compared CSF/ventricular and cranial meningeal panels with a cervical spinal meninges/roots dissection. It does not depict ventricular flow or cranial choroid plexus.

records.title: Spinal cord in cross-section: gray matter, tracts and roots
records.reason: Partial: Compared the cord diagram with transverse cord histology and a separate cervical root dissection. Histology does not identify colored tracts or roots; root photo is a different specimen/view.

records.title: Spinal nerve: roots, ganglion and rami
records.reason: The posterior spinal dissection explicitly identifies dorsal root/rootlets, ventral root, dorsal root ganglion and dorsal/ventral primary rami beside the cord. Section 35 provides the transverse cord relationship. The root/ramus image is a posterior dissection, not the drawing's axial view; cut-away vertebral tissues expose the nerves.

records.title: The four major plexuses and the phrenic nerve
records.reason: Partial: Compared body-wide plexus schematic with a visually inspected brachial-plexus photograph. Organism is not explicit on Calisphere record; cervical, lumbar, sacral and phrenic coverage absent.

records.title: Median, ulnar and radial nerves of the right upper limb
records.reason: Anterior arm dissection explicitly identifies median and ulnar nerves. Posterior arm identifies the radial nerve behind the humerus, and the posterior forearm shows the ulnar nerve near the elbow. Complementary dissections rather than one unbroken color-coded nerve map. The separately named plexus image supplies the proximal origin.

records.title: Femoral and sciatic nerves of the right lower limb
records.reason: Partial: Compared the femoral/sciatic diagram with a human sciatic-nerve file record. Sciatic photo itself was unavailable for visual inspection and no femoral nerve counterpart was confirmed.

records.title: Cranial nerves I-VI, inferior surface of the brain
records.reason: Inferior brain identifies olfactory tract, optic and oculomotor nerves; superior intracranial dissections show optic, oculomotor, trochlear, trigeminal and abducens nerves at the skull base. I–VI are covered by complementary inferior-brain and intracranial dissections, not one intact inferior brain photograph. Cut nerve segments are preserved in the dissections.

records.title: Cranial nerves VII-XII, brainstem and cerebellopontine angle
records.reason: Intracranial dissection 64 identifies facial and vestibulocochlear nerves; 65 identifies glossopharyngeal, vagus and accessory nerves; 66 identifies hypoglossal nerve. Inferior-brain image 58 also shows accessory nerve. The source shows cut nerves within an opened skull base rather than the schematic's intact brainstem/cerebellopontine-angle view.

records.title: Anterior eye: chambers, aqueous humor and zonules
records.reason: No source-page image was verified for a human anterior-segment specimen. A targeted NCBI eye-anatomy page fetch failed; no substitute drawing or model was accepted.

records.title: Retina: cell chain (schematic)
records.reason: Partial: Compared the retinal cell-chain schematic with a human photoreceptor-cell record. Image not visually inspected and one cell cannot represent layered retinal organization or ganglion/bipolar cells.

records.title: Middle ear: ossicles and windows
records.reason: Lateral wall dissection identifies tympanic membrane, malleus, incus and auditory tube. Medial wall views identify stapes, oval window with stapes footplate and round window. A left middle ear in opposing wall views, not the right coronal schematic. The auditory tube is named pharyngotympanic tube at the source.

records.title: Inner ear: vestibule, canals and cochlea
records.reason: Partial: Compared labyrinth schematic with human organ-of-Corti microscopy. Candidate image was not visually inspected and does not show vestibule, utricle, saccule or semicircular canals.

records.title: Cochlear ducts and the organ of Corti (schematic)
records.reason: Partial: Compared the duct/cell schematic with two human cochlear microscopy articles; the SEM organ-of-Corti surface was visually inspected. It does not show the whole duct compartments or complete schematic cross-section.

records.title: Smell and taste: pathways and receptor cells (schematic)
records.reason: Partial: Compared smell/taste panels with human olfactory mucosa micrograph metadata and OpenStax taste-bud micrograph metadata. Neither image was visually inspected; OpenStax taste tissue species is unstated and pathways/territories are absent.
requiredAnatomy: Facial nerve (VII): anterior tongue taste region
Glossopharyngeal nerve (IX): posterior tongue taste region

records.title: Sweat and sebaceous glands
records.reason: Final comparison: the inspected sweat-gland micrograph shows glandular profiles but its organism is unconfirmed and it does not show the full human eccrine/apocrine/sebaceous arrangement; Duke's human skin slide listing was not an inspected photograph. Human counterpart remains unsupported; absence is not established.

records.title: Original cell overview
records.reason: Final comparison: the broad cell schematic groups membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, nucleolus and multiple organelles, but no qualifying human source-page photo with visually checked organelle coverage and provenance is present in the reviewed candidates. Unavailable evidence, not evidence that none exists.

records.title: Original mitosis stages
records.reason: Final comparison: the schematic spans interphase through telophase; no source-page set in the reviewed candidates visibly verifies the full sequence in human cells. A single-stage image would not cover the stages. No qualifying set verified; not a claim that none exists.

records.title: Human kidney cortex specimen
records.reason: Final comparison: the displayed human kidney-cortex photomicrograph and file caption identify cortex with glomeruli/tubules; creator and file-specific CC BY-SA 3.0 terms are recorded. This is a direct specimen counterpart; stain/magnification are not inferred beyond the caption.

records.title: Alveolar sac specimen
records.reason: The exact Commons source page identifies a human alveolar-sac slide; its original image URL was retrieved and visually inspected, showing broad air spaces and septa. Creator Jpogi and CC BY-SA 4.0 terms are documented. This is a direct match for the assigned alveolar-sac specimen.

records.title: Simple squamous epithelium specimen
records.reason: Final comparison: the visible photo and caption identify human simple squamous epithelium; creator Naz Amann and CC BY 4.0 are stated on the file page. This single target is a direct match; no extra anatomy is claimed.

records.title: Simple cuboidal epithelium specimen
records.reason: The inspected human renal-cortex photograph shows cuboidal cells with round nuclei surrounding renal-tubule lumina. It is a specifically identified human example of the epithelial type, not a claim that the original unclassified photomicrograph has established species.

records.title: Simple columnar epithelium specimen
records.reason: Partial, not approved: Human ileal cross-section, villi and lymphoid tissue visible. The 2x overview does not resolve individual columnar epithelial cells, all crypt-cell types or the paired longitudinal wall view.

newPartialInspectionEvidence.observedAndLimitations: Human ileal cross-section, villi and lymphoid tissue visible. The 2x overview does not resolve individual columnar epithelial cells, all crypt-cell types or the paired longitudinal wall view.

records.title: Skin in section: layers, appendages and receptors
records.reason: Partial, not approved: Human thin skin; real tissue section opened. Human scalp; longitudinal follicles/bulbs and sebaceous glands visible. No claim that the overview resolves the complete papilla, sebaceous duct and arrector-pili combination. Human thick skin with a Pacinian corpuscle; no nail apparatus in the inspected field. Rejected as a nail-section match.

records.title: Simple epithelia: squamous, cuboidal, columnar (schematic)
records.reason: The verified human simple-squamous image supports one panel. A targeted University of Genoa simple-epithelia page contained human cuboidal kidney and columnar intestine photographs; both original images were visually checked. Its official terms state that site images/micrographs are protected and prohibit deep linking, so that page is excluded from eligible references. The human three-panel set therefore remains partial.

records.title: Pseudostratified and stratified squamous epithelia (schematic)
records.reason: Final comparison: checked nonkeratinized-stratified image has no confirmed human organism, while Duke's human skin slides were not visually inspected. Pseudostratified/ciliated and keratinized human panels remain unsupported; no complete counterpart.

records.title: Stratified cuboidal, columnar and transitional epithelia (schematic)
records.reason: Final comparison: inspected sweat-gland image is an unconfirmed-species example for a stratified gland duct only. It does not verify human stratified columnar or transitional epithelium; those panels remain unavailable.

records.title: Loose connective tissues: areolar, adipose, reticular (schematic)
records.reason: Final comparison: the BCC page lists areolar, adipose and reticular examples but individual source photo, species, creator/terms and visual content were not verified in the audited material. All three human panels remain unsupported.

records.title: Dense connective tissues: regular, irregular, elastic (schematic)
records.reason: Final comparison: Columbia source describes a human dense-regular tendon slide, but its photo was not visually inspected; no checked human images cover dense-irregular and elastic tissue. At most a text-level tendon lead, not a verified mapping.

records.title: Cartilages: hyaline, elastic, fibrocartilage (schematic)
records.reason: Final comparison: the BCC mammalian-histology page is a candidate for cartilage types, but no individual photograph, human specimen identity, creator/terms or image content was verified. Hyaline, elastic and fibrocartilage human panels remain unsupported.

records.title: Muscle tissues: skeletal, cardiac, smooth (schematic)
records.reason: Three individually named human references cover skeletal muscle, cardiac muscle and smooth muscle. Skeletal is electron microscopy, cardiac is light microscopy, and smooth muscle is a zoomable human uterine section; they are not matched stains, scale or section planes.

records.title: Nervous tissue: neuron and neuroglia (schematic)
records.reason: Final comparison: no reviewed candidate meets the public source-page, human provenance and image-inspection test for both neuron morphology and the represented glia. Evidence unavailable for this composite; not proof that no suitable images exist.

records.title: Nail in longitudinal section
records.reason: Final comparison: Duke describes a human fingertip slide, but no source photograph was visually inspected and nail plate, bed, matrix and fold structures were not confirmed. It is an index lead rather than a verified counterpart.

records.title: Composition of blood: plasma, serum and formed elements
records.reason: Final check: original human blood SEM was visually inspected; source caption and NCI metadata identify human circulating blood, erythrocytes, leukocytes and platelets, with Wetzel/Schaefer attribution and a public-domain note. Plasma/serum separation and clot/centrifugation panels remain unmatched.

records.title: Peripheral blood smear (schematic field)
records.reason: Final check: original human blood SEM now visually inspected and caption/provenance confirmed; it is a real human circulating-blood field, not a stained light-microscope smear or schematic-size comparison. Existing human May-Grünwald smear remains a distinct relevant example; this asset stays partial.

records.title: The five leukocytes, compared
records.reason: Final check: the human blood SEM image and file caption were inspected; its source description names lymphocyte, monocyte and neutrophil. Eosinophil and basophil are not shown/identified, so it supports only three of five types and remains partial.

records.title: Red bone marrow and hematopoiesis
records.reason: Final comparison: UNSW marrow histology photo was visually seen, but source does not establish species and its reuse terms are non-commercial; hematopoietic lineage/process schematic is not shown. No verified human counterpart.

records.title: Vessel wall layers and vessel types
records.reason: Final comparison: no reviewed source set provides visually inspected, human-confirmed photos for artery, vein, capillary and all depicted wall layers. This is unavailable source evidence, not proof of no public specimen images.

records.title: Flow chain: aorta to vein
records.reason: The continuous aorta-to-vein flow chain is a process diagram across scales, not a single static anatomical specimen. Real regional vessels remain photographable.

records.title: Three capillary types
